plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and the auction format (second-price sealed-bid), the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This is because any deviation from your true value can either lead to losing a profitable auction (bidding lower) or paying more than necessary (bidding higher). My value is $38, so I bid $38.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the payment rule (paying the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, and with three bidders, a conservative estimate of the second highest bid is around $6.7. However, my value is $35, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid a value close to my private value, but not exceeding it, to maximize profit.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the minimum increment. This is because any bid above zero has a chance of winning, and the payment is the *second* highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, and my value is $42, I want to win if possible, but minimize the payment. Bidding $0.1 ensures I win if others bid less, and the payment will be close to zero.
